name: Baltimore Oak Leaf 1832
foundry: Baltimore Type Foundry; F. Lucas, Jr., agent
description: A complete alphabet of shaded oak-leaf capitals, traced from the full reference sheet, including its leafy R. Capitals, ampersand and three punctuation marks; lowercase keys use capitals. No figures.
observed: All 26 capitals and & . , ! are direct traces of the complete Oak Leaf sheet hosted by Luc Devroye. The R follows that sheet, including its leafy lower leg. The retained Baltimore and Boston period specimens document the historical design and related impressions; they are not substituted for letters on the complete sheet.
reconstructed: No inferred letterforms, figures or additional symbols. Thresholding and cubic curve fitting interpret the sheet. Uniform glyph scaling, sidebearings and punctuation baseline placement are new digital metrics. Lowercase keys alias capitals. The intermediate publication of the complete sheet is unidentified; its historical attribution is accepted as the working source, not independently proven for every sort.

sources.title: Oak Leaf complete alphabet sheet, hosted by Luc Devroye; attributed to Baltimore Type Foundry, 1832
sources.rights: The underlying Oak Leaf design is documented in the 1832 Baltimore specimen and is public domain by age. The complete reproduction is hosted by Luc Devroye; its intermediate publication and reproduction history are unidentified. The attribution is the working basis for this revival. The project MIT license covers original digital work and does not assert ownership of the reference sheet.

revival.notes: Every visible encoded form has a measured crop in source/tracing.json. Normal builds use the canonical CFF master; optional preparation retraces the retained complete sheet.

character_set_notes: The complete reference sheet supplies A-Z and & . , ! only. Lowercase aliases the capitals; ordinary and nonbreaking spaces are blank. Figures and all other symbols are deliberately absent.
